traits.note: FNA vol. 28, Bryum (Spence; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants small, gregarious or in dense mats, white, silver-green, olive or green; stems 0.2-1(-2) cm, julaceous; leaves imbricate when dry, erect to erect-spreading moist, ovate, concave, 0.2-1(-1.5) mm; capsule inclined to pendent, (1-)2-3 mm; dioicous. Typical values are B. argenteum, the silver moss of pavements and roofs (same volume): white-green to silver-green, stems 0.2-1 cm, leaves 0.3-1 mm, hyaline in their distal quarter to half, apiculus short and hyaline; seta brown to red-brown 1-2 cm; capsule red to red-brown, ovate, 2-3 mm. Wikipedia, Bryum argenteum (read 2026-11-05): on pavement gaps, tarmac, concrete, walls and rooftops of cities, on disturbed nutrient-rich ground that dries out; leaves about 0.4 mm wide; capsules pendent.

traits.capsule_share.note: B. argenteum is dioicous; in towns it fruits only here and there, a few capsules a colony. Estimate.

traits.leaf_colour.note: The green lower blade; the silver comes from the hyaline tip (leaf_hyaline_share), drawn separately.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate for a pavement and roof turf that spreads also by bulbils; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.
